lessons.title: Get ready! What you will learn

pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 🔢 **Strand 1 — Number**
Counting, calculating and reasoning with numbers — the language of trade, science and everyday life.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B8.1.3)
- B8.1.3.1 — Apply the understanding of operations on fractions to solve problems involving fractions of given quantities and round the results to given decimal and significant places.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- review equivalent fractions, simplest form, mixed numbers and improper fractions
- add, subtract, multiply and divide fractions
- use the order of operations (BODMAS / PEDMAS) with whole numbers and fractions
- solve word problems involving fractions and percentages

pages.title: Reviewing fractions and the four operations
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Review fractions and solve problems involving basic operations on fractions.
Curriculum indicator B8.1.3.1.1
[[fig:m8-f08|Figure 3.1: 3/5 of the rectangle is shaded]]
## ✏️ Example 3.1
a) What fraction of the rectangle above is shaded? b) Write three fractions equivalent to [[4/7]]. c) Express [[18/24]] in simplest form. d) Express [[23/6]] as a mixed number. e) Express 2[[3/5]] as an improper fraction.
**Solution**
a) 6 of 10 equal parts: [[6/10]] = [[3/5]]
b) [[8/14]]**,** [[12/21]]**,** [[16/28]]
c) HCF of 18 and 24 is 6: [[3/4]]
d) 23 ÷ 6 = 3 remainder 5: 3[[5/6]]
e) [[2×5+3/5]] = [[13/5]]
## ✏️ Example 3.2
Work out: a) [[3/4]] + [[7/8]] b) [[4/5]] − [[1/6]] c) [[2/3]] × [[3/4]] d) [[5/8]] ÷ 2[[1/2]]
**Solution**
a) [[6/8]] + [[7/8]] = [[13/8]] = 1[[5/8]]
b) [[24/30]] − [[5/30]] = [[19/30]]
c) [[6/12]] = [[1/2]]
d) [[5/8]] ÷ [[5/2]] = [[5/8]] × [[2/5]] = [[1/4]]

pages.title: The order of operations
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Add and/or subtract, multiply and/or divide given fractions using the order of operations (BODMAS or PEDMAS) and apply the understanding to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B8.1.3.1.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: BODMAS / PEDMAS** — Work in this order: **B**rackets (**P**arentheses) → **O**rders (**E**xponents: powers and roots) → **D**ivision and **M**ultiplication, from left to right → **A**ddition and **S**ubtraction, from left to right.
> ⚠️ **Watch out!** Division and multiplication have **equal** priority — work from left to right. 18 ÷ 6 × 3 = 3 × 3 = 9, not 18 ÷ 18 = 1. The same is true of addition and subtraction.
## ✏️ Example 3.3
Simplify: a) 21 ÷ 3 + (3 × 9) × 9 + 5 b) 18 ÷ 6 × (4 − 3) + 6 c) 3^{4} ÷ 9 + 40 − 2^{3} × 3^{2} ÷ 9
**Solution**
a) Brackets: 3 × 9 = 27. Then 21 ÷ 3 = 7 and 27 × 9 = 243. So 7 + 243 + 5 = **255**
b) Brackets: 4 − 3 = 1. Then 18 ÷ 6 = 3, 3 × 1 = 3. So 3 + 6 = **9**
c) Orders: 81 ÷ 9 + 40 − 8 × 9 ÷ 9 → 9 + 40 − 8 = **41**
## ✏️ Example 3.4
Simplify: a) [[3/4]] + [[5/8]] × [[4/5]] − [[1/6]] b) [[3/4]] ÷ [[3/8]] + ([[4/5]] − [[1/2]]) c) ([[3/4]] + [[5/8]]) × [[4/11]] − [[1/2]]
**Solution**
a) Multiply first: [[5/8]] × [[4/5]] = [[1/2]]. Then [[3/4]] + [[1/2]] − [[1/6]] = [[9/12]] + [[6/12]] − [[2/12]] = [[13/12]] = 1[[1/12]]
b) Brackets: [[4/5]] − [[1/2]] = [[3/10]]. Divide: [[3/4]] × [[8/3]] = 2. So 2 + [[3/10]] = 2[[3/10]]
c) Brackets: [[6/8]] + [[5/8]] = [[11/8]]. Multiply: [[11/8]] × [[4/11]] = [[1/2]]. So [[1/2]] − [[1/2]] = **0**

pages.title: Word problems involving fractions
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Review word problems involving basic operations on fractions and related concepts.
Curriculum indicator B8.1.3.1.3
## ✏️ Example 3.5
Find a) the perimeter and b) the area of a rectangle measuring 1[[1/3]] cm by 3[[3/4]] cm.
**Solution**
a) P = 2 × ([[4/3]] + [[15/4]]) = 2 × ([[16/12]] + [[45/12]]) = 2 × [[61/12]] = [[61/6]] = 10[[1/6]] **cm**
b) A = [[4/3]] × [[15/4]] = [[60/12]] = **5 cm²**
## ✏️ Example 3.6
Faako answers 42 out of 60 questions correctly. What percentage of her answers are correct?
**Solution**
[[42/60]] × 100% = **70%**
## ✏️ Example 3.7
In a school, [[2/5]] of the learners eat from the school feeding programme, [[1/4]] bring packed lunch, and the rest go home to eat. What fraction go home for lunch?
**Solution**
1 − ([[2/5]] + [[1/4]]) = 1 − [[13/20]] = [[7/20]]
## ✏️ Example 3.8
Esi's orange drink was made of [[2/5]] orange squash and Fusena's was made of [[3/8]] orange squash. Whose drink tastes stronger of orange?
**Solution**
[[2/5]] = 0.4 and [[3/8]] = 0.375. Since 0.4 > 0.375, **Esi's drink** has a larger fraction of squash and tastes stronger.

pages.title: Exercise 3.3
pages.body:
> ✏️ **Exercise 3.3** — try these on paper or in your head, then tap **Quick check** to see the answers.
1. A farmer planted maize on [[3/8]] of his land and cassava on [[2/5]] of it. The remaining 9 acres were left fallow. How many acres of land does he have?
2. A tank holds 240 litres. It is [[5/8]] full. How many more litres are needed to fill it?
3. Kweku scored 38 out of 50 in Science and 44 out of 60 in Mathematics. In which subject did he do better? Use percentages.
4. A man spent [[1/3]] of his salary on rent and [[2/5]] of the remainder on food. If he had GH₵720 left, what was his salary?
5. Round [[22/7]] correct to 3 significant figures and to 4 decimal places.

pages.title: Chapter 3 summary
pages.body:
- Use a common denominator to add or subtract; multiply straight across; divide by multiplying by the reciprocal.
- BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication (left to right), Addition/Subtraction (left to right).
- "Fraction of the remainder" problems: work out what fraction is left at each stage.
